report:
Fresh final followup review of literal_syntax. Saved/read the prior complete report and inputs, started fresh, recaptured all three dependencies and compared every fragment. The sole difference is an unrelated implementation_references association comment in spec.rs. The claim, all five tests, source/BookFixture helpers and browser rendering dependency are unchanged. No literal-context or rendering behavior changed.

The full claim requires definition/heading/end-looking text to remain inert inside fenced/indented/inline code, escapes and raw/enclosing HTML, with standalone end comments active only outside those contexts. The ordinary parser association processes definition Text events only outside code/HTML states and enclosing tags; inline code is not Text, and odd preceding backslashes suppress escaped definitions. Heading closure requires an empty HTML stack. End-comment recognition requires a complete standalone HTML block outside enclosing tags. finish_anchor retains the original contiguous source, so treating examples literally preserves rather than deletes them. update_anchor_html_tags tracks enclosing elements across blank lines, handles quoted delimiters and multiline tags, skips comment/CDATA/processing-instruction bodies and invalid less-than text, and treats script/style/textarea/pre as raw text until their actual matching close. Stack updates resume real boundaries after closure. The new association comment does not affect this mechanism.

All five ordinary tests were read. boundary_examples_in_code_escapes_and_enclosing_html_are_literal asserts exact complete active content and exactly two real anchors for fenced/indented/inline/escaped examples, nested and multiline HTML, quoted false closing tags and inline-opened containers; parsing examples alone requires no definitions or diagnostics. malformed_looking_comments_are_content_and_do_not_end_claims preserves exact nonstandalone, nonexact, multiline and nested-looking comments until the real end. raw_html_text_does_not_hide_boundaries_after_its_closing_element covers script strings containing less-than/comment openers, style, textarea, pre and div text, requiring preserved body and recognition of the later genuine end/new definition. rendering_removes_only_parsed_end_markers checks direct and chapter rendering, exact removal span/count, preserved code/HTML/nonexact markers and outside prose. prose_rendering_hides_control_comments_but_preserves_literal_examples checks real control removal while retaining exactly three escaped literal examples, inline/fenced code markup and escaped HTML container.

Captured browser rendering uses shared role replacements and removes only recognized empty replacements before displaying remaining raw HTML literally, so it does not introduce an independent marker interpretation. The captured source and BookFixture helpers invoke production parsing/loading. No TODO/N/A entries or deferred clause exist. Every named context and resumption after actual HTML closure remain accounted for by current source and substantive assertions. This is a full claim assessment of the actual marker-only delta, with no other relied-on changes, rather than blind refresh. No source changes or test/build/browser execution occurred; fresh review commands and source inspection only. No requested edits.
